statement: For countable simple G of maximum degree D, p<1 and ||T_p||_2=M<infinity, independent sprinkling with epsilon D M<1 gives ||T_(p+(1-p)epsilon)||_2 <= M/(1-epsilon D M). For infinite connected quasi-transitive G and bounded T_pc with pc<1 this excludes uniqueness through pc+(1-pc)/(2DM), hence pc<pu.
assumptions: independent p and epsilon edge fields
quasi-transitivity for a positive uniform theta under uniqueness

statement: Exponential pointwise decay of Bernoulli bond connectivity does not imply boundedness of its l2 kernel. On the 4-regular Cayley tree tau_p(o,x)=p^dist(o,x), yet ||T_p delta_o||_2=infinity when p>=1/sqrt(3). At p=3/4 the radius-R squared row sum equals 1+(36/11)*((27/16)^R-1).
proof_or_counterexample: Unique path gives p^distance; sphere size is 4*3^(n-1); the resulting geometric series diverges when 3p^2>=1.
remaining_gap: No gap in the displayed elementary derivation; independent audit pending. This is not a counterexample to C0047 or to bounded T_pc.

statement: For infinite connected quasi-transitive G in Bernoulli bond percolation, if p1>pc and inf_(x,y) tau_p1(x,y)=0, then pu>=p1>pc. Pointwise monotonicity propagates the zero-infimum property to every q<=p1; FKG and almost-sure uniqueness would contradict it. This hypothesis is weaker than bounded T_p1, as demonstrated at p1=3/4 on the 4-regular tree.
assumptions: infinite connected locally finite quasi-transitive graph

statement: The sufficient Benjamini-Schramm 1996 spectral criterion includes the maximal-degree factor: k rho p<1 at a percolating p; k rho pc<1 suffices for pc<pu. On d-regular Cayley graphs this is pc||A||<1. The C0047-A001 attribution pc<1/rho with rho the random-walk spectral radius omits k.
